From soil data to decisions

I connect the full soil-information chain.

My work is strongest when the challenge cannot be solved by a single discipline: when field observations, laboratory measurements, environmental covariates, models, uncertainty and institutional delivery all have to work together.

Technical depth

Broad enough to connect systems. Deep enough to build them.

The combination is deliberate: strong pedological interpretation, modern sensing, geospatial computation and uncertainty-aware modelling are more valuable together than as isolated techniques.

Pedology & soil survey

Profile description, soil-landscape relationships, classification, field interpretation and survey logic.

Digital soil mapping

Covariate engineering, spatial modelling, continuous and categorical predictions, validation and scalable map production.

Sampling design

cLHS, environmental-space optimisation, spatially balanced designs and survey strategies under real field constraints.

Soil spectroscopy

Vis–NIR and MIR workflows, spectral libraries, calibration transfer and scalable soil characterization.

Remote & proximal sensing

Optical imagery, proximal measurements, bare-soil information and integration of multi-source environmental data.

Machine learning & AI

Random forests, gradient boosting, ensembles, quantile prediction and AI-enabled geospatial workflows.

Uncertainty & validation

Prediction intervals, quantiles, confusion-based measures and validation strategies designed for decision confidence.

Soil information systems

Data harmonisation, interoperable workflows, national architectures and transformation of technical outputs into usable services.

Scientific programming

R, reproducible geospatial workflows, large raster processing, model pipelines and automation for operational soil science.

Research vision

Understand what soils remember — and what that means for their future.

My scientific trajectory spans soil mineralogy, spectroscopy, remote sensing, digital soil mapping and soil carbon. The emerging question that connects them is how present-day soil observations encode past processes and improve prediction under environmental change.

Research frontier · Soil Memory
Can we decode the history stored in soils to predict how they will respond next?

Soils integrate long-term signals of parent material, climate, vegetation, hydrology, land use, disturbance and management. I am developing a research direction around soil memory: combining pedological knowledge, spectroscopy, remote sensing, temporal observations and AI to reconstruct trajectories and improve prediction of future soil functioning in a changing climate.
